summary.headline: Aelea Commodities H2 FY26 standalone revenue Rs 189.50 cr with 13.10% EBITDA margin and Rs 12.35 cr PAT; FY26 revenue up 112% to Rs 363.12 cr.
summary.overview: Management reported H2 FY26 standalone revenue of Rs 189.50 cr, EBITDA of Rs 24.82 cr (13.10% margin) and PAT of Rs 12.35 cr (6.52% margin), versus losses a year earlier. For FY26, standalone revenue rose 112.07% to Rs 363.12 cr, EBITDA was Rs 40.20 cr (11.07% margin) and PAT Rs 21.19 cr, with EPS of Rs 10.40 versus Rs 0.65. Consolidated FY26 revenue was Rs 381.50 cr (up 109.46%) and PAT Rs 21.32 cr. The call was dominated by a 10-year (FY37) strategy presentation, with the Q&A focused on higher finance costs, working capital and inventory build, CNSL plant timing, and FY27 guidance, which was not quantified.

segments.name: Cashew kernel processing (core)
segments.commentary: Processes raw cashew nuts (RCN) into wholes and pieces; average mix 63% wholes and 37% pieces, with average kernel realisation of about Rs 590-595/kg. Around 16,000 tonnes of RCN processed in H2 and a similar volume in H1. About 95% of raw material is African-origin, sourced via merchant traders.

segments.name: CNSL / by-products (oil extraction, solar)
segments.commentary: CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT is under construction, with management guiding to benefits from around H2 FY27 and a product-level EBITDA margin of about 10%. Rooftop solar is installed; ground-mounted solar awaits government approval. B2C consumer pouches are about 1% of sales.

guidance_outlook: FY27: management expects top-line and bottom-line growth at rates similar to FY26, but declined to give a revenue number; an analyst's Rs 500 cr FY27 revenue figure was not confirmed.
FY28: too early to comment; management said it will revisit after about six more months of work.
EBITDA margin: management says the company normally operates at around 10-11% EBITDA margin, which it says it has broadly met.
Finance cost: management expects it to stay at similar or higher levels as the company deepens its value chain, and said absolute figures will grow with scale.
CNSL plant: construction nearly complete with about 30 days of works remaining; commissioning depends on government approvals. Phase 3 capex is expected later in the year.
B2C: targeted at roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin in the long run, pursued through a product basket rather than e-commerce.
capex_capacity: Capacity scaling from 40 MT/day to 140 MT/day, which management says is backed by IPO proceeds; current utilisation about 94-95%.
Phase 2 (CNSL) capex is already committed and underway, with only a small amount pending; Phase 3 capex is expected in the later part of the year.
Ground-mounted solar is pending government approval because of changes to norms for consuming solar power; rooftop solar is complete.
Long-term 2037 strategy targets 1,000 MT/day cashew capacity, plus almond, walnut, pistachio and makhana processing (makhana with a 50-tonne capacity plan).
A Maharashtra cultivation project and capex was flagged by an analyst as not updated; management said it is still being worked on and not crystallised.
demand_pricing: Management said processing is constrained by raw-material quality rather than machine capacity; the company says it fully used its enhanced capacity during H2.
Raw-material sourcing has moved deeper into the value chain (direct sourcing at about 60-65%), which lifted margins but raised working capital and finance costs.
Geopolitical disruption: longer sea transit from Africa, currency swings of around 50 paise a day, and higher RCN price volatility, with no material price impact yet.
Institutional clients are a stated priority for longer-term visibility, but institutions are about one-fifth the size of general trade in the market.
Inventory rose to about Rs 100 cr and management expects it to increase further with growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise from about Rs 2 cr to Rs 8 cr?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company moved deeper into the value chain, where suppliers do not give credit, but margins are better. Finance cost is expected to stay at similar or higher levels.

qa_highlights.question: What is FY27 and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 growth is expected to be similar to FY26 in rate, with no numbers given. FY28 comment deferred about six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNSL plant timeline and contribution?
qa_highlights.answer: Construction nearly complete with approvals pending; benefits expected around H2. Management said CNSL adds EBITDA rather than top line, at about 10% product-level EBITDA margin.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capacity utilisation and RCN volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Utilisation is about 94-95%. About 16,000 tonnes of RCN were processed in H2, roughly the same as H1.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sourcing mix between Africa and India?
qa_highlights.answer: About 95% of processing is African-origin, sourced through merchant traders based in Singapore or Dubai, and 5% is local.

qa_highlights.question: What is the B2C strategy and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: B2C is about 1% of sales. Management said it will grow organically rather than through heavy marketing, targeting roughly 13-15% EBITDA margin on a product basket.

risks_watch: Working capital and finance cost: rising short-term borrowing and inventory (about Rs 100 cr) as sourcing deepens; management gave no debt-to-equity red line.
CNSL and ground-mounted solar commissioning depends on government approvals, which have no fixed timeline.
Geopolitical and shipping disruption from Africa, with longer transit and higher currency and RCN price volatility.
Management declined to quantify FY27 or FY28 numbers; watch whether growth matches the stated similar rate.
Related-party or structural details on the Maharashtra project remain unclear and not yet crystallised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the 10-year strategy and FY26 results, but evasive on forward numbers: it repeatedly declined to give FY27 or FY28 figures, the Maharashtra project and timelines, and it deflected on B2C sales and the cause of higher finance cost.
key_quotes: So, for FY27, we are likely to continue our growth rate.

At the end of the day, it's cashew and you, me, or whoever goes at buying it would like to see what is the per gram, per 100 gram price and compare it with wherever you are, other source of buying is.
So we have roughly 95% of the entire processing depending on the African origins only.

CNSL extraction facility of above 50 MT under construction; construction nearly complete with ~30 days of works left, commissioning depends on government approv

growth.why: Management guides FY27 top-line and bottom-line growth similar to FY26's ~112% but gave no number, and the 40-to-140 MT/day capacity scale-up is backed by IPO proceeds with no timeline; utilisation is 94-95% and the CNSL plant (2 quarters away, pending approvals) is minor.
